correctness.rationale: For a norming image sequence, weak compactness gives a weak limit. A unit weak limit yields a one-dimensional initial space; otherwise a Riesz extraction from normalized weakly-null differences yields an infinite-dimensional even-subsequence span with infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement. A partial isometry S from that span into its orthogonal complement has S²=0 and m_G(SG)=1. Cauchy–Schwarz gives w(S)≤1/2 and near-norming dual vectors are at Hilbert distance less than sqrt(2δ) from Gx, yielding v_G(SG)≤1/2. Scalar codomain gives exact equality of defining suprema. The 2x2 identity supplies sharpness. The argument requires no compactness or norm attainment of G.

value.rationale: Settles the explicit infinite-dimensional Hilbert relative-spear question in a complete structural form, not merely a special case: the codomain dimension is the exact criterion. The sharp uniform half-gap is quantitative, and the proof handles non-norm-attaining operators via a nontrivial Riesz splitting lemma. It distinguishes a relative seminorm problem from the classical operator-norm numerical index.
